title: Probationary fallback windows & slew-rate circuit for region/tier routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During regional spikes we see rapid flip-flopping of fallback decisions (route -> fallback -> restore -> route) which increases downstream load and causes degrading UX. Existing threshold-based circuits trigger too aggressively on transient 429 bursts and don't account for rate-of-change. Goal: implement a probationary fallback window combined with a slew-rate based trip score to smooth decisions across region and tier routing and to provide safer automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants.

Design summary:
- Signals: 429 rate, request timeouts, 5xx error rate, p95/p99 latency, and token-weighted error contribution.
- Probationary window: when a signal crosses a soft threshold, mark the region/tier as "probationary" for a configurable window (default 30s) before actuating fallback. During probation the router applies conservative throttles and increases sampling for telemetry.
- Slew-rate trip scoring: compute a short-term derivative (error_rate change per 10s) and combine with absolute error rate to yield a trip score. This prevents instant trips on sudden but small bursts and prioritizes sustained degradation.
- Hysteresis + decay: once tripped, circuit enters a cooldown period with exponential decay of trip score; a smaller recovery threshold is required to return to normal to avoid oscillation.
- Tier-aware policies: primary, secondary, and archival tiers have separate thresholds and decay rates. Tenant-critical routes use stricter criteria and shorter probation windows.
- Model-variant fallback: fallback policy picks the lowest-cost compatible variant that satisfies the current latency SLO, with optional KV-cache-only fallbacks when model switching isn't possible. Map of compatibility lives in model catalog.
- Safeguards: soft-fallback (rate-limited to X requests/sec), global kill-switch feature flag, and auto-escalation alert when fallback rate > 5% for > 10m.

Instrumentation & metrics to add: fallback.probation_count, fallback.trip_score.{region,tier}, fallback.actuation_rate, fallback.recovery_time, fallback.token_weighted_error, fallback.slew_rate, fallback.canary_errors, and per-tenant fallback_rate. Dashboards + alert rules to be added in Console (routes/fallbacks).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Probation window prevents at least 60% of previously-observed flip-flop episodes in the 2-week historical test trace with no increase in user-visible error rate.
2) Trip score correlates with sustained degradations: simulated sustained 5xx spikes (5 minutes) must cause trip; short bursts (<=15s) must not.
3) Canary rollout: feature flag canaryed to ~5% of traffic and toggled off automatically on >2x baseline errors.
4) Dashboard shows new metrics and runbooks with clear thresholds for Pager and SRE responses.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1: Unit + integration tests for trip_score logic (local), add metrics emitters (PR #1).
- Phase 2: Staged canary: internal teams + 5% production via feature flag for 48h. Monitor fallback.actuation_rate and canary_errors.
- Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% with staged increases (20% -> 50% -> 100%) with 24h observation windows.

Notes: This approach complements, not replaces, our existing circuit-breaker framework. We'll provide backward-compatible config knobs in the routing policy API and default sensible values for hosted customers.
